visuals.heading: What Internship and Full-Time Actually Mean

items.text: The average pre-placement offer conversion rate across Indian internships sits around 20-25%, which means most internships do not turn into the job.
An internship earns its place in your plan when it passes a specific set of tests, not when it simply exists on offer.
A recognisable employer name shortens the trust gap with the next recruiter, whether or not the internship converts to a PPO there.
A shipped feature, a completed campaign, a dataset you cleaned and analysed, a deck you presented to a real stakeholder.
On the other side of the same decision, some internships are structured to extract free or near-free labour rather than to build a career.
No contract, no offer letter, no written stipend agreement
Internships in India are not covered by a single dedicated law the way apprenticeships are, and interns generally are not treated as employees under labour statutes.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Decide

items.text: The four questions keeps this decision grounded in the specific offer in front of you instead of a generic "internships are good" or "always take the full-time job" rule that ignores the details.
Ask for the internship's actual task list before you accept, not the job-title description.
A recruiter who cannot describe three concrete tasks you will do in week one usually does not have a real program built.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That Waste a Placement Season

items.text: These specific mistakes consistently cost people either a real offer or months of unpaid effort that built nothing lasting.
Accepting any internship just to have a line on the resume
A vague, unpaid internship with no defined tasks does less for your resume than a part-time paid role, a personal project, or a certification with real output.

blocks.heading: Decision Plan for the Next Stretch

items.text: Move through these steps at whatever pace genuinely fits your situation.
List every internship and full-time option you are actually considering, and run each one through the four questions before comparing stipend or salary numbers alone.
For each internship option, ask directly about last batch's PPO conversion rate, mentor assignment, and whether tasks are defined in writing.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The PPO conversion math nobody explains upfront

rows: Roughly one in four to one in five interns receive a pre-placement offer. This is the number to anchor your expectations to, not the exceptional cases you hear about.
Some internship batches convert only one in ten interns. A low conversion rate is not always a red flag on its own, check headcount growth and team budget before reading it as rejection.

Large, well-funded tech employers running structured summer internship programs report conversion in this range because the internship functions as an extended, paid interview for a role that already has budget.

visuals.title: Figures in Context

items.text: It skips the actual PPO conversion math, leaving people to assume an internship is a near-guaranteed path to a job when it converts roughly one time in four or five.
It rarely explains that internships sit largely outside India's formal labour protections, so the responsibility to check terms falls on the intern, not on assumed regulation.
It frames a full-time offer as automatically "playing it safe," ignoring cases where the offer itself is weak and a strong internship would build more long-term value.

blocks.heading: How to Evaluate a Specific Internship Offer

items.text: What will my day-to-day tasks actually be, in specific terms, not a generic job title.
Who is my assigned manager or mentor, and how often will they review my work.
What is the stipend, and is it confirmed in writing.
What percentage of the last batch received a pre-placement offer, and how large was that batch.
What is the defined start and end date, and the expected weekly hours.
